Appeal No.645/2024 Appellant:- Sonal Jain, W/o Rohit Jain, Aged about 29 years, R/at No.10, 6th Floor, Ganesh Apartment, Thenginamarda Matade Lane, Cottonpet Main Road, Bengaluru. (By: Smt. N.K., , Advocate) Vs. 2 Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 Respondents:- 1) Rohit Jain, S/o Late Hiralalji Tated, Aged about 26 years, R/at No.159-227/1 and 228, Pampti Plaza, 2nd Floor, Gowlinguda, Chaman, Nampally, Telangana. 2) Ranidevi @ Pammidevi Tated, W/o Late Hiralalji Tated, Aged about 45 years, R/at No.159-227/1 and 228, Pampti Plaza, 2nd Floor, Gowlinguda, Chaman, Sonal Jain vs Rohith Jain on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65219610/ 1 Nampally, Telangana. 3) Heena Tated, D/o Late Hiralalji Tated, Aged about 25 years, R/at No.159-227/1 and 228, Pampti Plaza, 2nd Floor, Gowlinguda, Chaman, Nampally, Telangana. 4) Rahul Tated, S/o Late Hiralalji Tated, Aged about 27 years, R/at No.159-227/1 and 228, Pampti Plaza, 2nd Floor, Gowlinguda, Chaman, Nampally, Telangana. 3 Crl. texts.facts: This is an appeal filed u/s 29 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (hereinafter referred as PWDV Act,) preferred by the appellant/petitioner against the orders passed in Crl.Misc.No.65/2024 dated 18/03/2024 on the file of MMTC-II, Bengaluru, by denying an order of ex-parte interim maintenance and also dismissing the petition as against respondent No.2 to 5 in the petition filed under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. Rank of the parties is referred to as per their ranks assigned before the trial court. 3. The facts of the case leading to this appeal may be summarized as under; The appellant is a 29 years old house wife with a bachelor degree in Arts from Rajasthan, born in Bengaluru and brought up in Rajasthan, her family moved to Bengaluru in December 2019, she married to respondent No.1 on 02/12/2022, it was an arranged marriage held in a resort called Sonal Jain vs Rohith Jain on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65219610/ 2 'Green Paradise' at Surat, Gujarath, respondent No.1 runs a wholesale business of sale of certain household and gift items in Hyderabad, respondent No.2 is mother, respondent No.3 is sister, respondent No.4 is brother and respondent No.5 is brother's wife, all are residing together in Hyderabad, petitioner and respondents are Marwadi Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 Jains by faith and they live in large joint families, after marriage, petitioner was taken to respondents house, where she was subjected to extreme repeated physical and verbal abuse by respondent No.1 at the instigation of respondent No.2 to 5, there were at least 17-18 such instances of severe physical abuses between 5 th December 2022 till 28th June 2023, there were countless daily incidents of emotional, economic, verbal abuse which lead to mental sufferings of petitioner, she was ruthlessly subjected to harassment at the hands of respondents, one such incident was just after 15 days of the marriage, when petitioner had gone to beauty parlor with respondent No.3 i.e. her sister-in-law where she spent an extra amount of Rs.500/- on her care, the same was complained by respondent No.3 to respondent No.1 which lead to beat up the petitioner as punishment for spending an extra amount, there were small and trivial Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 issues which used to be resulting in physical and verbal abuses on the petitioner by respondent No.1, while respondent No.2 to 5 used to watch and enjoy the same, whenever petitioner requested respondent No.2 to 5 to interfere in the matter, they used to tell her that it is his right to do so and they cannot interfere in this, there always used to be pin pricks from respondent No.2 to 5 and at their instigation respondent No.1 always subjected the petitioner to immense physical, mental and emotional stress, as such though she had conceived for twins during the first week of March 2023, she could not retain her pregnancy due to the mental stress caused on her by the respondents which resulted in miscarriage in the month of May 2023, petitioner was beaten in the middle road by respondent No.1, there was no proper medication during her ill health, in the month of May 2023 respondent No.1 had taken the petitioner to Goa Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 trip for five days, by that time as they were going back to Bengaluru, when petitioner asked to purchase sweets for her family, respondent No.1 lost his control, started physically harassing her by pulling her hair and dragging her to the hotel bathroom and continuously slapped on her face at least 5-6 times with all his strength, on 24/06/2023 respondent No.2 snatched her food plate while she was eating and abused her to go hungry for which respondent No.1 assaulted her by abusing that she has to obey all the instructions of respondent No.2, on 28/06/2023 for rituals petitioner was brought to Bengaluru by her brother Hitesh Kumar as there is a ritual that newly wedded bride need to return to her parents house and stay there for about 2 months, petitioner had planned to return to her matrimonial house after two months without disclosing the domestic violence and abuse suffered by her at her matrimonial Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 house, however by slip of tongue petitioner had to disclose one of the incident, thereafter at the instance of her family members she had to disclose all the harassment which was faced by her in the matrimonial house and she also expressed that she is scared to go back to the respondents house. 4. It is further stated that, severity of physical and emotional abuse and manipulation inflicted by respondent No.1, his mother, his sister on the petitioner was so much that she had shaken to the core, it was extremely fearful and she was psychologically and physically traumatized, upon knowing all these incidents petitioner's family members asked her not to return to her matrimonial house, out of fear and for her safety, thereafter brother of petitioner who is also an advocate made efforts to reconcile the matter which was of no use, the respondents made several conditions to take the Crl. Sonal Jain vs Rohith Jain on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65219610/ 3 Appeal No.645/2024 petitioner back to matrimonial house subject to seeking apology with respondent No.2 i.e. mother-in-law over phone, despite the same petitioner was subjected to physical and mental harassment, respondent No.2 also threatened the petitioner to get divorce from her and to perform 2nd marriage to her son and the respondents have posed condition to take petitioner back subject to signing on several papers by her and her family members, as such, the respondents have also assaulted the sister of petitioner and her brother-in-law when they had been to their house for reconciliation of the matter, thereafter respondent No.2 to 5 having failed in their tactics to hide their atrocious act started pressurizing respondent No.1 to convince petitioner not to act against them and to take any legal course of action along with posing several threats to defame her, thus respondents Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 continuously abused and threatened the petitioner for several months. 5. The petitioner being abandoned by her husband having no financial means to maintain herself has been forced to move to her parents house where already her aged parents, brother and his family are living, there was also life threat to the petitioner, as such, petitioner unable to go back to her marital house, though she wishes to reside in a separate house she is unable to do so as she has no income of her own to maintain herself, therefore she requires maintenance for food, clothes, shelter and other expenses by pleading that respondents are financially well having multiple source of income and respondent No.1 and 4 jointly run and own a wholesale and retail business for sale of local and imported household items and gift items in Hyderabad making a net profit at lease Rs.50 lakhs p.a., also respondent No.2 Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 owns 4 BHK flat in Hyderabad with house hold assets such as gold and silver worth of Rs. 3 crores, has four 2 wheeler and two cars viz., Maruthi Suzuki Ertiga and one Volvo approximately worth Rs.3 crores, and stock at warehouse amounting Rs.3,50,00,000/-, respondents have kept all the valuables and school records of the petitioner in their house, therefore she filed a complaint before the court under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against respondents seeking several orders such as protection order, maintenance etc., and also sought for interim maintenance, the same was not considered by the trial court by its order dated 18/03/2024 holding the issue of notice to respondent No.1 is necessary before granting any order of interim maintenance and also dismissing the petition as against respondent No.2 to 5 on the ground that there is no prima facie materials to establish the Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 alleged domestic violence, hence the petitioner being aggrieved by the order of trial court has preferred this appeal by urging the following grounds; a) Impugned order of the trial court suffers from complete non application of mind, perverse and arbitrary, lacks in reasoning, hence liable to be dismissed. b) The impugned order of dismissal of the petition as against respondent No.2 to 5 is an erroneous order though there are several allegations made against respondent No.2 to 5 at para 11, 13, 15 to 16, 20, 21, 23, 25, 26, 45 to 48, the trial court erred in considering the fact that, respondent No.2 to 5 were residing with the petitioner in a joint family as they are from the conservative back ground of Marwadi Jain community, respondent No.3, 5 and petitioner used to be in the kitchen together and to do household chores together, they were gathering complaints about the petitioner in Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 order to divulge respondent No.1 so that he could physically discipline her. The trial court failed to consider the object of Section 3 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 which includes verbal, emotional and economic abuses and failed to take note of the fact that the allegations made against respondent No.2 to 5 in the application falls within the definition of domestic violence and faild to consider that there are more than prima facie of abuse by the respondents, not just warranting an issuance of notice to respondent No.1 alone, it requires notice on all the respondents. Appeal No.645/2024 respondent No.2 to 5 which is contrary to pleadings averred in the petition . e) The trial court erred in considering the fact that the petitioner lived in her matrimonial house from the date of marriage i.e. December 2022 till June 2023 and she was subjected to physical, verbal and mental abuse, same was direct result of having lived in a shared household and having a domestic relationship with all the respondents, as such the impugned order dated 18/03/2024 is erroneous in law. f) Thus, the petitioner by relying on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Crl. Petition No.4710/2024 prayed to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned order passed by the trial court and to restore the dismissal order as against respondent No.2 to 5, also sought for an ex-parte order for Rs.70,101/- interim maintenance as sought in I.A. No.1/2024 and also for return of valuable Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 articles and documents of the petitioner as sought in I.A. No.2. On these grounds petitioner prays to allow the appeal as mentioned above with a request to remit the matter back to the trial court for consideration. 6. After registration of the appeal, notice was issued to the respondents, they appeared through their counsel. Appeal No.645/2024 necessary to go through impugned order and reasons for such order
texts.arguments: 14. It is canvassed on behalf of the petitioner that, respondents are Marwadi Jains, they normally live in joint families and the same has not been denied by the respondents also. In the written arguments submitted on behalf of respondent No.1 to 5, it is canvassed that, the order of the trial court is just and proper, there are no prima facie materials to show the commission of alleged Sonal Jain vs Rohith Jain on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65219610/ 6 domestic violence on the petitioner as held by the Hon'ble Apex court in case of Shyamlal Devda and others Vs. Parimala. Further in a reported decision Shyamlal Devuda and others Vs. Parimala the Hon'ble Apex court has held that, while issuing a notice to the respondents the court has to be prima facie satisfied that there are prima facie materials to show that the respondents have caused an act of domestic violence against the petitioner. However, on going through the afore quoted decision i.e. Shyamlal Devda and others Vs. Parimala, it is specifically mentioned that, there has to be prima facie materials to show the commission of domestic violence as against the wife by the husband or his family members. 16. In this connection, the learned counsel for the petitioner has relied on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Crl.
